channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Canadian Dollar languishes near two-week low as bullish USD offsets oil gains ahead of Fed
item.description: The USD/CAD pair retains its positive bias for the sixth straight day, trading near the 1.3930 area, a two-week high during the Asian session on Wednesday amid a bullish US Dollar (USD).

item.title: WTI slips to near $100.50 despite escalating Middle East supply disruptions
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price declines after two days of gains, trading around $100.50 per barrel during Asian hours on Wednesday. However, crude oil prices may rebound, driven by a series of broadening supply disruptions across the Middle East.

item.title: Saudi air defenses intercept Houthi drone near Mecca
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition said that Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Yemen’s Houthi group near Mecca, Reuters reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen flatlines ahead of Fed rate decicion
item.description: The USD/JPY pair holds steady near 155.25 during the early Asian session on Wednesday. Traders prefer to wait on the sidelines ahead of the US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate decision later on Wednesday. On Friday, attention will shift to the Bank of Japan (BoJ) interest rate decision.

item.title: Gold declines below $4,300 as US yields climb, Fed rate decision looms
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) declines to near $4,285 during the early Asian session on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar softens as risk-off mood meets FOMC countdown
item.description: The Aussie Dollar loses 0.11% against the Greenback on Tuesday as risk appetite remains negative amid calls from AI company CEOs to slow development, while the FOMC monetary policy meeting looms. Expectations for a Fed rate hike undermine the AUD/USD, which trades at 0.7130.

item.title: The Euro edges lower as Frankfurt's hike takes effect the day Washington votes
item.description: EUR/USD closed Tuesday near 1.1540, down 0.1%. It fell on the day the European Central Bank (ECB) raised its deposit rate to 2.50% and in each of the three sessions since.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Rebounds above 207.00 as oversold risk eases
item.description: The GBP/JPY edges higher by about 0.29% on Tuesday, even as risk appetite has shifted to the sour side due to geopolitical developments that are driving global bond yields higher amid inflation fears. At the time of writing, the cross-pair trades at 209.02 after bouncing off daily lows of 208.25.

item.title: The Pound drifts lower as the Fed lines up a rate above the Bank of England's
item.description: GBP/USD closed Tuesday near 1.3470, down 0.2%. Wednesday's Asian and London hours are the last before the Fed is expected to raise its rate for the first time since July 2023. By the New York close its ceiling should sit a quarter-point above Bank Rate.

item.title: Mexican Peso retreats as USD/MXN bounces from near YTD low
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) loses some ground against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, with USD/MXN rising by over 0.09% amid a sour market mood and a stronger Greenback, ahead of the FOMC monetary policy decision on Wednesday. The exotic pair trades at 17.15, after hitting a daily low of 17.10.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar slides ahead of Fed’s decision
item.description: NZD/USD trades close to the 0.5760s, extending a run of losses that has dragged it toward the lower end of its recent range. A broadly firmer US Dollar (USD) is behind the slide, with the greenback supported by climbing United States (US) yields and rate-hike expectations.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range-bound with slight downside bias against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: Quek Ser Leang at UOB notes USD/CNH remains directionless, trading narrowly around 6.71 with little change in momentum. Intraday, the pair is expected to hold between 6.7060 and 6.7160.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Bears crack 100-day SMA, eye 1.1500
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends its losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, sliding below the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at 1.1555, opening the door to further downside, with sellers setting their sights on Monday’s low of 1.1523.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Market tests Indonesia policy credibility – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts report that USD/IDR extended gains as investors assessed the appointment of Suahasil Nazara as Indonesia’s new Finance Minister, the third in under two years.

item.title: Crude Oil rallies again as Saudi Arabia's route around Hormuz shuts
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Crude Oil trades just above $100.00, up about 3% on the day. It is on track for a third straight weekly gain.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Slow appreciation with weak demand – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that Chinese growth remains export-led as domestic demand stays soft, with investment and retail sales under pressure and car sales slumping.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar firms as markets brace for Fed rate decision
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) gained to 99.60 mark on Tuesday, and the bond market drove the move.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Downtrend seen limited against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD extended gains toward 1.2725 as the US Dollar strengthened broadly and Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) stayed around 1.65% above its mid-point.

item.title: Japanese Yen slips as Oil lifts yields ahead of the Fed
item.description: USD/JPY trades near 155.20 on Tuesday, rising for a second straight day and pulling away from the roughly seven-month low it set last week. A firmer US Dollar (USD) is doing the work, helped by a sharp jump in Oil that has pushed US Treasury yields higher.

item.title: China: Growth risks rise with softer demand – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Hunter Chan and Shuang Ding assess China’s July-August data and conclude that domestic demand weakened while production held up.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Bears break 0.5800 as Kiwi slide deepens
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) tumbles against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday for the second straight day this week, down 0.37% as risk appetite sours, with AI company CEOs expressing concerns about the rapid pace of evolution and as high energy prices push markets to expect further tightening by the

item.title: 100 threshold: United States Dollar Index faces make-or-break Fed decision
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) holds firm near a two-week high on Tuesday as traders prepare for the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy decision on Wednesday. At the time of writing, the index trades around 99.66, up 0.17% on the day.

item.title: Gold bulls hit 100-day SMA wall as US yields bite
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price holds firm on Tuesday, capped on the upside by solid resistance at the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at $4,328, while broad US Dollar strength and elevated US bond yields weighed on the non-yielding metal.

item.title: South Korean Won: Supportive fundamentals, slower gains – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s FX analysts Charlie Lay and Moses Lim note that the Korean Won has rallied nearly 15% against the Dollar since late June, driven less by the current account surplus and more by structural shifts in flows.

item.title: Canadian Dollar remains vulnerable aas Fed takes centre stage
item.description: USD/CAD extends its advance for a fifth consecutive day on Tuesday, hovering near a two-week high as the US Dollar (USD) stays firmly supported ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement on Wednesday.

item.title: Silver attempts cautious rebound ahead of closely watched Fed decision
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $63.40 on Tuesday at the time of writing, up 0.28% on the day. The white metal attempts to stabilize as investors refrain from taking large positions ahead of the United States (US) Federal Reserve (Fed) monetary policy decision on Wednesday.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average slides as yields beat the Fed to tomorrow's hike
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades just under 52,000, down around 450 points, a day before the Fed's first expected hike since July 2023. Bets in the futures market put the odds of a quarter-point at 92.5%, so Wednesday's vote is not the news.

item.title: British Pound wilts as Oil shock sends US yields past 5%
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) edges lower by some 0.07% against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, with the latter enjoying inflows due to its haven status amid fears of a possible Oil supply shortage. The GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3487, after peaking at around 1.3505.

item.title: Gold finds support near one-month low ahead of Fed interest rate decision
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trims part of its intraday decline on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro stays neutral against Pound ahead of UK inflation data
item.description: EUR/GBP trades in the mid-0.8500s, unable to reclaim the 0.8600 barrier on Tuesday as the Euro (EUR) has struggled even after the European Central Bank (ECB) raised its three key rates by 25 basis points (bps) on September 10, lifting the deposit rate to 2.50%.
